newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish president stalls cheap farming fuel bill.
newsitem.headline: Polish president stalls cheap farming fuel bill.

text.p: Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski challenged on Thursday a controversial bill which allows farmers to buy diesel fuel at below market prices, and sent it to the Constitutional Tribunal, his press office said.
The office said in a statement that the president doubted whether the bill, passed by parliament earlier this year, was compatible with the constitution.
To become law, Kwasniewski has to sign the bill but instead he has referred it to the tribunal, a court which considers the constitutionality of legislation approved by parliament.
Kwasniewski thought the bill gave the finance and interior ministers too much freedom in deciding how to control purchases and use of the cheap fuel, the statement said.
The bill would exempt farming diesel from part of the excise tax during the next four years. The cheap fuel would be coloured and its use for non-agricultural purposes would be prohibited.

The bill was heavily criticised by the finance ministry, which said the draft, which would cost the budget about 600 million zloty ($185 million) in lost revenue, would unfairly privilege farmers over other groups.
The Polish Peasant Party (PSL), the smaller group in the ruling leftist coalition, put forward the bill, saying it would make farm production more profitable and help the sector's restructuring.
Some analysts have said the bill was meant by the Peasant Party to boost its rural support in parliamentary elections due on September 21.
If the Constitutional Tribunal rules that the bill is unconstitutional and the president then vetoes it, parliament would need a two thirds majority to push it through.
